title: Do Mezzanines, Penthouses and Roof Terraces Count as Floors? (2027)
desc: How to count a house's floors under Circular 34/2026/TT-BXD: when mezzanines and rooftop penthouses are excluded, attic floors, semi-basements, why it matters.
summary: Circular 34/2026/TT-BXD on counting storeys: a house mezzanine of no more than 65% of the floor area below, and a rooftop penthouse of no more than 30% of the roof floor area, are not counted as floors.
body: p

“A 3-storey house with a penthouse”, “a 2-storey house with a mezzanine” – these familiar descriptions may differ from how floors are counted under the rules. The number of floors affects the construction grade, whether you may design it yourself or must hire a design firm, and the permit procedure. The current guidance is in Appendix II of Circular 34/2026/TT-BXD (effective from 1 July 2026, Article 4).
h2
1. How are the types of floor defined?
p
Under the notes to Table 2 of Appendix II (Circular 34/2026/TT-BXD):
ul
Above-ground floor: a floor whose floor level is higher than or equal to the ground level at which the building sits.
Basement: a floor with more than half its height below the ground level at which the building sits; semi-basement: half its height is at or above ground level.

Mezzanine: an intermediate floor whose slab lies between two floors with main functions (or between the roof and the floor immediately below), with a floor area smaller than the main-function floor immediately beneath it.
Attic floor: located within a pitched-roof space, with vertical walls (if any) not higher than 1.5 m above the floor slab.
Penthouse (tum) floor: the topmost floor used to enclose the stairwell, lift shaft and equipment and to give access to the roof slab and for rescue.
h2
2. How the number of storeys is counted
p
Number of storeys = the sum of above-ground floors and semi-basements, excluding attic floors. The penthouse and mezzanine are excluded only in the following cases (note 4 to Appendix II):
ul
A penthouse floor is not counted when the penthouse slab area is no more than 30% of the roof slab area.

The mezzanine of a private house (including a house combined with another civil purpose) is not counted when the mezzanine floor area is no more than 65% of the construction floor area of the main-function floor immediately below, and only one mezzanine may be excluded.
p

So a “roof terrace” – the open part of the roof slab – is not a floor; but if you build an enclosed room on the terrace beyond the extent of the penthouse (more than 30% of the roof slab area), it no longer qualifies for exclusion as a penthouse and counts towards the number of floors.
h2
3. Examples
ol
A 2-storey house with a 60 m² roof slab and a 15 m² stair penthouse (25%): the penthouse is not counted → 2 floors.
The same house, but with an altar room and laundry room on the roof totalling 25 m² (about 42%): the penthouse exceeds 30% → counted as 3 floors.
A townhouse with a ground floor of 80 m² and a 50 m² mezzanine (62.5%): the mezzanine is not counted. If the mezzanine is 60 m² (75%), it counts as a floor.
A house with a semi-basement garage: the semi-basement is counted in the number of storeys.
h2
4. Why does the number of floors matter?
ul

Who may design: owners may organise the design themselves only when the house has fewer than 3 floors, no basement, total floor area under 250 m² and height under 12 m (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).

Construction grade: number of floors, height and total floor area are grading criteria; the grade is used to determine permit-issuing authority, permit-exempt cases, the warranty period and so on (Clause 1, Article 3). See How the grade of a private house is determined.
Permit: the permit-exemption conditions for a private house include a criterion of fewer than 7 floors (Point g, Clause 2, Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025).
h2
5. Note: floor area is still counted in full
p

Mezzanines and penthouses are not counted in the number of floors but are still counted in total floor area: total floor area includes basements, semi-basements, mezzanines, technical floors, attic floors and penthouses; the floor area of each floor includes the enclosing walls, loggias, balconies and stairs (note 2 to Appendix II). Building height is measured to the highest point including the penthouse or pitched roof.
p

note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal texts. The floor-counting method above follows Appendix II of Circular 34/2026/TT-BXD (used to determine the construction grade); local planning and architectural regulations may have their own rules on building height, so check the planning information where the land is located.
